name: CARE (2013) with aesthetic-medicine extensions
source_note: Item wording paraphrased from the CARE checklist (Gagnier et al., 2013; care-statement.org). Before submission, download the official checklist the target journal requires and transfer locations onto it.

items.item: The words "case report" plus the phenomenon of greatest interest (complication, indication, population, technique).
aesthetic: Name the product class or device type, not only the brand (e.g., 'poly-L-lactic acid' rather than a trade name alone).
items.ask: What is the single most important message of this case — the complication, the new indication, the special population, or the technique? I will build the title around it.

items.item: 2–5 keywords identifying the diagnoses or interventions in this case, including 'case report'.
aesthetic: Include the material/device class and the anatomical region (e.g., 'hyaluronic acid filler', 'tear trough').
items.ask: Any keywords you want included (e.g., for indexing in a specific journal)? Otherwise I will propose 5.

items.item: Introduction: what is unique about this case and what it adds to the literature.
items.ask: In one sentence, what do colleagues learn from this case that they did not know before?

items.item: Main concerns of the patient and important clinical findings.
Primary diagnoses, interventions and outcomes.
Conclusion: the main take-away lesson(s).
Brief background summarising why this case is unique, with relevant medical literature.
aesthetic: State how often this event/indication has been reported before (result of the novelty search).
items.ask: Did you run (or should I run) a PubMed search for prior reports? How many similar cases were found?

items.item: De-identified demographics (age, sex, ethnicity, occupation if relevant).
aesthetic: Fitzpatrick skin type.
Ethnicity/ancestry when relevant to pigmentation or anatomy.
items.ask: What is the patient's Fitzpatrick skin type?

items.item: Main concerns and symptoms of the patient.
aesthetic: The aesthetic goal in the patient's own words, and expectations.
items.ask: What was the patient's main aesthetic concern and goal, ideally in their own words?

items.item: Medical, family and psychosocial history, including relevant past interventions and outcomes.
aesthetic: Full prior aesthetic-treatment history: products/devices, areas, dates (at least the last 12–24 months).
Unknown or non-registered fillers disclosed as such.
Relevant medications: anticoagulants, isotretinoin, GLP-1 receptor agonists, immunomodulators.
Autoimmune disease, keloid tendency, herpes history, recent vaccination or infection when relevant to the event.
Body dysmorphic disorder screening result (if performed).
items.ask: Prior aesthetic treatments (what, where, when)? Relevant medications (anticoagulants, isotretinoin, GLP-1 agonists, immunomodulators)? Autoimmune disease, recent infection/vaccination? Was BDD screening done?

items.item: Relevant physical examination and other clinical findings.
aesthetic: Validated severity scale at baseline (site-specific scale, GAIS baseline not applicable).
Standardised photographs: views, lighting, distance, camera/imaging system (e.g., VISIA, 3D).
For complications: size, consistency, tenderness, colour, fluctuance, distance from injection points.
items.ask: Which baseline scale scores and imaging (VISIA/3D/ultrasound) exist? Were photos standardised (same lighting, distance, views)?

items.item: Historical and current information organised as a timeline (table or figure).
aesthetic: Day 0 = index treatment; include every treatment session, onset of any event, each intervention for it, and each follow-up visit.
items.ask: Please confirm the dates (or day offsets) of: index treatment, symptom onset, each management step, and each follow-up visit.

items.item: Diagnostic methods (examination, lab testing, imaging, questionnaires).
aesthetic: High-frequency ultrasound / Doppler findings, culture, histopathology, biofilm work-up where relevant.
items.ask: Were ultrasound, Doppler, culture, or biopsy performed? What did they show?

items.item: Diagnostic challenges (access, financial, cultural).
items.ask: Were there any diagnostic challenges (e.g., imaging unavailable, patient declined biopsy)?

items.item: Diagnostic reasoning including differential diagnoses.
aesthetic: E.g., inflammatory vs non-inflammatory nodule; product vs biofilm vs foreign-body granuloma; Tyndall effect vs oedema vs bruising.
items.ask: What differential diagnoses did you consider and why were they excluded?

items.item: Prognostic characteristics where applicable.
Types of intervention (pharmacologic, surgical, preventive, self-care).
Administration of intervention (dosage, strength, duration).
aesthetic: Injectables: product (generic + trade name, manufacturer, country), lot number if relevant, volume/units per site and total, dilution/reconstitution (PLLA: diluent volume and hydration time; toxin: U per mL), injection plane, needle vs cannula and gauge, technique (bolus/linear/fanning/microdroplet), entry points.
Energy-based devices: device model and manufacturer, wavelength, fluence, pulse width, spot size, passes, overlap, cooling, endpoints.
Complication management: hyaluronidase units and dilution, steroids/antibiotics (drug, dose, duration), laser/drainage details.
Operator qualification and experience.
items.ask: Please give the full treatment parameters: product/device, dose or energy settings, dilution, plane, needle/cannula gauge, technique, number of sessions and intervals, and the operator's experience.

items.item: Changes in intervention, with rationale.
items.ask: Was the plan changed at any point (dose, product, extra session)? Why?

items.item: Clinician- and patient-assessed outcomes.
aesthetic: Clinician: GAIS / site-specific scale, ideally by a blinded independent evaluator.
Patient: satisfaction or FACE-Q module.
Objective: VISIA / 3D volume / ultrasound thickness, same settings as baseline.
items.ask: Who rated the outcome (treating physician, independent blinded rater, patient)? Which scales/instruments at which time points?

items.item: Important follow-up diagnostic and other test results.
Intervention adherence and tolerability (and how assessed).
aesthetic: Downtime, pain, swelling, bruising duration.
items.ask: How long was downtime? Pain/bruising/swelling and how long did they last?

items.item: Adverse and unanticipated events.
aesthetic: Report even minor events; state 'none' explicitly if none occurred.
Length of follow-up at which the absence of events is claimed.
items.ask: Any adverse or unexpected events at all (including minor)? What was the total follow-up duration?

items.item: Strengths and limitations in the management of this case.
aesthetic: Single case, unblinded assessment, confounders (weight change, concurrent treatments, season/sun exposure for pigmentation).

items.item: Discussion of the relevant medical literature.
Rationale for conclusions (including assessment of possible causes).
aesthetic: For complications: causality assessment (temporal relationship, alternative explanations).

items.item: Primary take-away lessons of this case report.
The patient shares their perspective or experience whenever appropriate.
aesthetic: Satisfaction, psychological impact, willingness to repeat treatment.
items.ask: Can you provide a short statement from the patient about their experience (or should this section be omitted)?

items.item: Did the patient give informed consent? Provide if requested.
aesthetic: Separate written consent for publication of identifiable facial photographs; eye bars do NOT de-identify a face.
Off-label use: consent for the off-label treatment itself and ethics committee approval if required.
items.ask: Is there written consent for publication, specifically covering facial photographs? Was any use off-label, and if so is there ethics approval?
